column1: # redact.tsv — what `./setup.sh report` REDACTS, declared once, as data.
#   Design record: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-setup-ledger-selfcheck-design.md,
#   D10.3 (`./setup.sh report` is how a defect travels) and D11 (the `report`
#   row, from Replicated troubleshoot.sh's redactors: redaction happens IN
#   PROCESS, as each section is collected, from a declared default list).
#   WHY IT IS A FILE. The report is built to be pasted into a chat, and until
#   P2 its only protection was a scan that REFUSED the whole report when a
#   credential value appeared in it — so a single value turning up in a
#   container log cost the operator the entire report, at exactly the moment
#   they needed it. Now every section is piped through one filter that replaces
#   what this file declares, and the scan stays behind it as the last line of
#   defence (the guard nobody else has). The filter and the scan read THIS
#   list — plus questions.tsv's `secret` column — so they cannot disagree about
#   what a secret is. A missing or key-less copy of this file makes the report
#   REFUSE rather than run unredacted: it is release content.
#   COLUMNS, tab-separated, `-` where a field is empty:
#     kind       key   = `pattern` is a bash GLOB over .env KEY NAMES. The VALUE
#                        of every matching key is replaced, wherever it appears,
#                        with [REDACTED:<KEY NAME>] — by bash's own substitution
#                        inside a read loop, so a value never reaches an argv
#                        (`ps` shows argv). Values shorter than eight characters
#                        are skipped: `none`, `0` and `1` are legitimate answers
#                        and a substring of half the English language
#                shape = `pattern` is an EXTENDED regular expression (sed -E)
#                        for a credential SHAPE, redacted whether or not .env
#                        knows the value. Static release content, so it may sit
#                        in sed's argv. Applied AFTER the key rows, so a value
#                        .env knows keeps its more useful key-name label
#     pattern    the glob (key) or the ERE (shape). A shape may not contain a
#                tab or the \001 byte (the filter's sed delimiter)
#     replace    shape rows only: the sed -E replacement (\1 = the first group).
#                `-` for key rows, whose replacement is always [REDACTED:<KEY>]
#     doc        one plain sentence: what the row catches, and why
#   tests/test_single_report_redacts.py parses this file and plants a value of
#   every kind in the report's sources.
# kind
key
column4: Every password .env holds — the databases', Neo4j's, Exchange's — named by the shape make-secrets.sh and questions.tsv give them.

column1: key
column4: Every token: the Jira/Confluence API tokens, the façade and sandbox-runner tokens.

column1: key
column4: Every key: the proxy's admin key, LiteLLM's salt key, n8n's encryption key, the upstream LLM key, the spine's own virtual key.

column1: key
column4: Any client secret an integration adds, so a new one is covered before anybody remembers to list it.

column1: key
column4: The spine's minted LiteLLM virtual key — named on its own because it is the credential the three historic leaks were.

column1: key
column4: The proxy's master key, which can reconfigure the proxy — named on its own for the same reason.

column1: shape
column4: A user:password@ in any URL — a database connection string echoed into a log carries one.

column1: shape
column4: An HTTP bearer token, as a request log or a curl -v trace prints it.

column1: shape
column4: A LiteLLM (or OpenAI-style) virtual key's sk-... shape, from a proxy or container log that names one .env never held.
